title: Eleven Entries and One Shared Bench
subtitle: 公平与尊重 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 公平与尊重（做人与做事·公平对待与尊重他人）
meta: 主题语境：公平与尊重（做人与做事·公平对待与尊重他人）　|　核心词汇：discrimination　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 discrimination 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the lexicographer ① defined a discrimination that no dictionary in the city would have printed, and he said the defining was the whole of the entry. The ② discrimination, meaning the distinction and not the bias, ran eleven entries and stayed unmarked in the proof; a discrimination, he said, is the only thing in a dictionary that is judged by how long it is left unillustrated.

Every ③ discrimination in that dictionary had the same shared bench in the example under it, and the ④ discrimination at the end, meaning the one they kept for the law reports and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever illustrated twice. A discrimination, his assistant said, is nine parts example and one part somebody willing to define; the lexicographer said the example is the part that fills eleven entries.

The teacher meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the discrimination was the whole of the lesson, meaning the bias and not the distinction. The ⑥ discrimination, meaning the bias and not any of that, is the only thing in a lesson that everybody names and nobody wants; discrimination, she said, is either something you define or the only word that means both a distinction and a bias. She said the bias is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ discrimination had become a line in a glossary, and the glossary had become an argument about the shared bench. The ⑧ discrimination of the whole thing, the lexicographer wrote in March, was one dictionary and eleven entries of defining; discrimination, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to define. She said the defining was never mentioned.

The ⑨ discrimination I remember is the one at the end, which was illustrated in 1976 and is still described as the clearest in the dictionary. A ⑩ discrimination, the assistant said in 1978, is the only thing that improves by being explained; every discrimination, she said, is a bias that has agreed to look like a distinction. She said the bias was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 区别；辨别（指词典里释义的那一条）
B. n. 辨别（指那份区分本身，与那种偏见相对）
C. 固定搭配：define a discrimination 界定一条区别
D. n. 辨别（指留给法律文献用例的那一条）
E. n. 辨别；区分（抽象总称，指一部词典的辨别之功）
F. n. 辨别（指术语表里写到、被收录的那一条）
G. n. 歧视；偏见（指课堂上被点名的那种看法）
H. n. 偏见（抽象总称，指人人叫得出名却无人想要的那种）

items.q: defined a discrimination that no dictionary in the city would have printed
The discrimination, meaning the distinction and not the bias
the discrimination was the whole of the lesson
the discrimination had become a line in a glossary
The discrimination of the whole thing
A discrimination, the assistant said in 1978

answers.why: define a discrimination 意为“界定一条区别”，1954 年词典编纂者界定了一条全城没有一部词典肯印的区别。
discrimination 意为“辨别”，指那份区分本身而不是那种偏见，它历经十一个词条而在校样上没有标注。
discrimination 意为“区别、辨别”，指那部词典里每一条区别，每一条下面的例句里都是同一条共用的长凳。
discrimination 意为“辨别”，指留给法律文献用例的那一条，是唯一有人配过两次例句的。
discrimination 意为“歧视、偏见”，指课堂上被点名的那种看法，老师说这种偏见就是那堂课的全部。
discrimination 意为“偏见”，指人人叫得出名却无人想要的那种而不是那份区分，是课堂里人人都叫得出名、却无人想要的东西。
discrimination 意为“辨别”，指术语表里写到、被收录的那一条，到 1962 年这条区别成了术语表里的一行。
discrimination 意为“辨别、区分”，编纂者三月写道，整件事的辨别之功是一部词典和十一个词条的界定。
discrimination 意为“辨别”，我记得的是末尾那一条，1976 年配上例句，至今仍被说成词典里最清楚的一条。
discrimination 为抽象总称，助手 1978 年说，一条区别是唯一会因为被解释清楚而变得更好的东西。
